hints: Express the double-angle cotangent in terms of $t=\tan\theta$.
Use $\cot2\theta=\dfrac{1-t^2}{2t}$ and set it equal to $2t$.
Solve the resulting equation for both signs of $t$, then find all angles in $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Express $\cot 2\theta$ in terms of $\tan 2\theta$ using $\cot A = \dfrac{1}{\tan A}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{\tan 2\theta} = 2\tan\theta$$

Apply the tangent double angle identity $\tan 2\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$:
$$\dfrac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{2\tan\theta} = 2\tan\theta$$

Take the square root of both sides:
$$\tan\theta = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \approx \pm 0.447214$$

Solve for $\theta$ in the range $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
- In Quadrant I (where $\tan\theta > 0$):
$$\theta_1 = \alpha \approx 24.095^\circ \approx 24.1^\circ$$
- In Quadrant II (where $\tan\theta < 0$):
$$\theta_2 = 180^\circ - \alpha \approx 180^\circ - 24.095^\circ = 155.905^\circ \approx 155.9^\circ$$

State both solutions rounded to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 24.1^\circ, \quad 155.9^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Applies trigonometric formulae to derive an equation in $\tan\theta$, or equivalent in sines/cosines; Solves for $\theta$; Concludes with $\theta=24.1^\circ$ or $155.9^\circ$.
